notes: El envio de KDA entre chains distintas ya no dice que ha fallado cuando en realidad va en camino, y ensena el identificador del pacto desde el primer momento. El envio en si no cambia. / Sending KDA between different chains no longer reports a failure when the transfer is actually on its way, and it shows the pact identifier from the start. The transfer itself is unchanged.

notes_i18n.es:
EL CROSS-CHAIN DECIA QUE FALLABA CUANDO NO FALLABA
Mandar KDA de una chain a otra son dos pasos y la app tiene que esperar a que el primero entre en la cadena. Esa espera era de un minuto. En la red real un bloque tarda unos treinta segundos, asi que cualquier retraso normal agotaba el plazo y salia en rojo «El paso de salida no se mino», con el envio perfectamente en marcha. Comprobado en la cadena: el dinero llegaba igual.

Lo caro no era el susto, era lo que venia despues: creyendo que no habia salido, la gente lo mandaba OTRA VEZ.

QUE CAMBIA
La espera pasa de un minuto a cinco. Si aun asi no consta, ya no se llama fallo: sale un aviso en naranja que dice que va en camino y que NO se reenvie. Un fallo de verdad de la cadena sigue saliendo en rojo y con su motivo, que son cosas distintas y ahora se distinguen.

EL IDENTIFICADOR YA NO SE PIERDE
Cada envio entre chains tiene un identificador (pactId) y es lo unico con lo que se remata si algo se corta a mitad. Antes, si vencia la espera, se tiraba sin llegar a ensenarlo. Ahora aparece en cuanto la salida esta en la cadena, y se ve dentro del propio dialogo de envio en vez de detras de el.

EL DINERO NUNCA SE PIERDE
Si el segundo paso no llega a darse, lo que se envio queda en el pacto y se remata luego con ese identificador. Eso era verdad antes y lo sigue siendo; lo que faltaba era decirlo con claridad y dar el numero.

EL ENVIO NO SE TOCA
Misma firma, mismas comisiones, mismas carteras. Esta version cambia lo que la app cuenta, no lo que la app hace.
notes_i18n.en:
CROSS-CHAIN REPORTED A FAILURE THAT WAS NOT ONE
Sending KDA from one chain to another takes two steps, and the app has to wait for the first one to land on chain. That wait was one minute. On the real network a block takes about thirty seconds, so any normal delay ran out the clock and showed a red "the outgoing step was not mined" while the transfer was perfectly under way. Verified on chain: the money arrived anyway.

The costly part was not the scare, it was what came next: believing it had not gone through, people sent it AGAIN.

WHAT CHANGES
The wait goes from one minute to five. If it still does not show up, it is no longer called a failure: an orange notice says it is on its way and asks you NOT to send it again. A real on-chain failure still appears in red with its reason - they are different things and are now told apart.

THE IDENTIFIER IS NO LONGER LOST
Every cross-chain transfer has an identifier (pactId), and it is the only thing that lets you finish it if something is cut short halfway. Before, if the wait expired, it was thrown away without ever being shown. It now appears as soon as the outgoing step is on chain, and inside the send dialog itself rather than behind it.

THE MONEY IS NEVER LOST
If the second step does not happen, what you sent stays in the pact and can be completed later with that identifier. That was true before and still is; what was missing was saying it clearly and handing you the number.

SENDING ITSELF IS UNTOUCHED
Same signing, same fees, same wallets. This version changes what the app tells you, not what the app does.
